title: One event, three messaging models
summary: A queue, a topic and a log treat the same message differently.

steps.n: The producer sends a job to the queue and one worker will take it.
Once the worker acknowledges, the queue deletes the message for good.
The same producer publishes an event and every subscriber receives its own copy.
The event is appended to the log with an offset and stays for the retention period.
A new consumer starts at an older offset and reads history that the queue no longer holds.
Billing and search each keep their own offset in the log and read at their own speed.

title: A duplicate delivery made harmless
summary: The consumer checks a message id before applying the effect.

steps.n: The broker delivers a message with a stable id to the consumer.
In one transaction the consumer inserts the id and updates the data.
The acknowledgement is lost on the network, so the broker thinks the work failed.
The broker delivers the same message again after the timeout.
The insert finds the id already recorded, so no row is inserted.
The consumer skips the effect, acknowledges, and the customer is charged only once.

title: A message routed by a topic exchange
summary: The exchange copies the message into every queue whose binding matches.

steps.n: The producer publishes to the events exchange with routing key order.paid.eu.
The topic exchange compares the key with each binding pattern.
The billing binding order.paid.# matches, so a copy enters the billing queue.
The search binding order.# also matches, so it receives a copy too.
A queue bound to refund.# does not match and gets nothing.
The billing consumer takes the message and acknowledges it when done.

title: Retry then park a failing message
summary: A delayed retry queue limits attempts and a parked queue holds the rest.

steps.n: The queue hands the consumer up to its prefetch limit of messages.
The consumer cannot process one message because the payload is malformed.
The consumer rejects it and the broker dead-letters it into the retry queue.
The retry queue holds it for 30 seconds before it expires.
On expiry the message is dead-lettered back to the main queue for another attempt.
Once the attempt header reaches the limit the message goes to the parked queue for a human.

title: A keyed record reaches its partition
summary: The same key always lands in the same partition so order is kept.

steps.n: The producer sends an order event with the key order-4411.
The partitioner hashes the key and takes it modulo the partition count.
Partition 2 is led by broker 1, so the record is sent there.
The followers on broker 2 fetch the record and copy it to their logs.
With acks=all the leader answers after enough replicas have the record.
The next event for order-4411 hashes to the same partition and keeps its order.

title: A consumer group rebalance
summary: Partitions move when a member joins, and consumption pauses briefly.

steps.n: Consumer 1 is alone in the group and reads all six partitions of the topic.
Consumer 2 starts and sends a join request to the group coordinator.
The coordinator tells members to stop and rejoin, so reading pauses.
The coordinator assigns three partitions to each consumer.
Consumer 2 receives partitions 3 to 5 and Consumer 1 keeps 0 to 2.
Each consumer resumes from the last committed offset of its partitions.

title: Leader failure with a healthy ISR
summary: A caught-up follower becomes leader, so no acknowledged record is lost.

steps.n: The producer writes a record and waits for in-sync replicas to confirm.
The follower fetches the record and stays in the in-sync set.
The record is acknowledged only after min.insync.replicas have it.
The leader broker stops, and the partition has no leader for a moment.
The controller promotes the follower, which already has every acknowledged record.
The producer finds the new leader and carries on without data loss.

title: Log compaction keeps the latest value
summary: Older records for a key are removed in the background.

steps.n: The producer appends user-1 = A, user-2 = B, then user-1 = C to a compacted topic.
A background cleaner reads closed segments and finds duplicate keys.
It removes user-1 = A because a newer value exists.
The producer writes user-2 with a null value to delete that key.
After the delete retention time the cleaner removes the key itself.
A new consumer reading from the start sees only the latest value per key.

title: Spotting and fixing consumer lag
summary: Lag is read per partition, then traced to a cause.

steps.n: Monitoring shows partition 1 is 18 minutes behind while the others are current.
The operator finds the consumer for partition 1 alive but stuck on one slow call.
Broker metrics look normal, with no under-replicated partitions.
The consumer waits for a downstream API that has become slow.
The operator adds a timeout and a retry limit, then restarts the consumer.
The consumer catches up and lag in minutes returns to near zero.

title: Fan-out with a topic and queues
summary: One publish reaches several queues, each with its own dead-letter queue.

steps.n: The service publishes the order event to the topic.
The topic delivers a copy to the billing queue.
A worker receives the message and it is hidden from others for the visibility timeout.
After the maximum receive count the message moves to the dead-letter queue.
An alarm on the dead-letter queue depth notifies the team.
After the bug is fixed the team redrives the parked messages back to the billing queue.

title: A schema change checked in CI
summary: The registry refuses a change that would break existing readers.

steps.n: The developer changes a field name in the schema file.
CI sends the new schema to the registry's compatibility check.
The registry reports that renaming the field breaks backward compatibility.
The pull request cannot merge, and the message says which rule failed.
The developer adds the new field with a default and keeps the old one.
The registry accepts the change as compatible.
Consumers keep reading old and new records while the old field is retired later.

title: Failure and recovery: messages dropped by an exchange
summary: A routing key typo loses messages without any error.

steps.n: The producer starts publishing with the key order.payed.eu after a code change.
The topic exchange finds no queue bound to that key.
With no alternate exchange the message is silently discarded.
The consumer sees nothing wrong and simply receives fewer messages.
The operator follows one order id and finds it published but never delivered.
The exchange shows a rising unroutable count that matches the missing orders.
The producer is corrected and an alternate exchange is added to catch unroutable messages.
The missed orders are republished from the outbox, and an alert is set on the dropped count.

title: Failure and recovery: Kafka disk fills up
summary: A traffic spike outruns retention and brokers stop accepting writes.

steps.n: A bug in a producer sends twice the normal volume of records.
The topic keeps data for seven days, so disk use climbs far faster than planned.
The log directory fills and the broker marks it failed and stops.
Producers receive errors because partitions have no available leader.
The operator lowers retention on the noisy topic so old segments are deleted.
The buggy producer is rolled back and a quota is added for it.
With space available the broker starts, replicas catch up and partitions come back.
Consumers continue from their committed offsets with no gaps in the data.
